records.subject: s_the_call
records.value: system

records.subject: s_the_call
records.value: A single strict chain, ordered by date, oldest first. Water is not shared and not divided in a shortage: it is served in order until it runs out, and the last man in the order gets nothing rather than a little. The one number in this system is a year, and it is not power — it is a place in a queue. A 1461 cannot lift a stone, cannot fight, cannot heal; it can only be earlier than you.

records.subject: s_the_call
records.value: A woman puts her hand on a wet iron wheel, says a year out loud, and four miles downstream the water in somebody else's furrow turns and walks backwards out of the field.

records.subject: s_the_call
records.value: The spoken date at an open headgate, in earshot of a witness the register will accept.

records.subject: s_the_call_nature
records.value: The chain is not neutral. It rewards the ones who were there first, forever, and it was built by people who arrived first with horses.

records.subject: s_the_call_view
records.value: view

records.subject: s_the_call_view
records.value: A woman puts her hand on a wet iron wheel, says a year out loud, and four miles downstream the water in somebody else's furrow turns and walks backwards out of the field.

records.subject: s_the_call_view
records.value: The register prints the order. It does not print how many of the oldest dates are held by the same four families through wives and cousins, and the index that would show it was rebound in a different order.

records.subject: r_first_in_time
records.value: In a shortage the river is served in date order, oldest first, until it is gone. There is no dividing, no averaging, and no mercy written anywhere in the procedure.

records.subject: r_first_in_time
records.value: The watermaster reads eleven names off a board and stops reading. The twelfth family is standing right there and hears the reading stop.

records.subject: r_first_in_time
records.value: Two identical fields a fence apart sell at ten times the difference, and the difference is a year written on a paper neither buyer will ever be able to change. Land agents do not walk the ground; they read the book and never leave town.

records.subject: r_first_in_time
records.value: A trial is a genealogy. Nobody argues about need, harm, or use — they argue about which sheet of paper is older, and the whole profession is paleography with a bailiff.

records.subject: r_first_in_time
records.value: Children are introduced by date before name. A betrothal is announced as a merger of two dates and the year is said louder than either family.

records.subject: r_beneficial_use
records.value: A right exists only while it is being used for something the register will consent to write down. Water called and not spent is water you have just proved you do not need.

records.subject: r_beneficial_use
records.value: A man floods four acres of a crop no market wants, in front of witnesses, on a day the town is short, and everyone understands and hates him and would do the same.

records.subject: r_beneficial_use
records.value: The commonest offence in the basin is waste for show — and the second commonest is its inverse, hiring somebody to swear they saw a field dry when it was wet.

records.subject: r_beneficial_use
records.value: An entire trade of use-makers: contractors who grow thirsty, worthless, deliberately spectacular crops on other people's land purely to keep a date breathing, paid by the acre-foot and never invited to dinner.

records.subject: r_beneficial_use
records.value: A sect that holds spending is the only sacrament and thrift is the only sin — their rite is opening a gate onto stones and letting it run all night, and their houses smell of wet rock.

records.subject: r_forfeiture
records.value: Five running years without a recorded use and the right falls out of the chain. Everyone below it moves up one place, automatically, without a hearing, on the day the fifth year closes.

records.subject: r_forfeiture
records.value: A clerk draws one line through one row and the room behind him gets louder, and out at Ninefold somebody who has never called in her life will get water this August.

records.subject: r_forfeiture
records.value: A dry decade is a redistribution. The basin is governed less by who can call than by who can survive not calling, and every council is a truce between people counting each other's fifth years.

records.subject: r_forfeiture
records.value: Sabotage aimed at capacity rather than water — burn the crop, lame the horse, break the arm that opens the wheel. Nobody attacks a ditch. They attack the ability to use one.

records.subject: r_forfeiture
records.value: The sick and the very old are watched with an attention that looks like devotion. An invalid who cannot walk out to a headgate is a vacancy, and the neighbours who bring soup are also counting.

records.subject: r_the_dryness
records.value: The call is spoken and it takes payment out of the speaker. For the season after a call, the caller's own body runs dry — no sweat, no tears, no milk, no spit worth the name.

records.subject: r_the_dryness
records.value: A widow stands at her husband's grave with a cracked mouth and dry eyes while the whole town watches, and the town knows exactly what she chose in July.

records.subject: r_the_dryness
records.value: Callers are known on sight by split lips and the salt tin they carry, and there is a whole etiquette of not offering them anything to eat that needs chewing.

records.subject: r_the_dryness
records.value: Grief has to be performed some other way, so the basin's funerals are loud — hired weepers, a drum, and the dry-mouthed family standing still in the middle of the noise.

records.subject: r_the_dryness
records.value: An army cannot call and march. Callers travel wrapped in wet cloth in wagons at the back, useless for anything but the one thing, and every campaign in the basin is planned around keeping four people from cracking.

records.subject: cr_priority
records.value: criterion

records.subject: cr_priority
records.value: ordinal

records.subject: k_no_date
records.value: Bare thumb, and a cord at the belt with the knot cut out of it. Shopkeepers serve you last and do it without malice, the way you would let a wall go by.

records.subject: k_no_date
records.value: Free, and the free thing is the point: everyone starts here and most stay, and the ones who stay learn to be useful to callers as the only trade left.

records.subject: k_junior_date
records.value: A cord with one knot, worn outside the coat. In a good year you eat; in a dry year the knot is a joke people make in front of you.

records.subject: k_junior_date
records.value: Bought with everything a family has, or granted new by the register for breaking new ground — and the new ground has to be watered and shown wet within one season or the date dies where it was written.

records.subject: k_working_date
records.value: A brass sleeve on the cord, green at the edges. People finish sentences differently when it comes into a room — they stop and start again shorter.

records.subject: k_working_date
records.value: Paid for in use: the holder must call and spend water every year in a way the register will write down, which means growing thirsty worthless crops in years nobody needs a crop, in public, while neighbours go short watching.

records.subject: k_senior_date
records.value: A thin black iron ring on the thumb, the stamped numbers worn to a smoothness. A caller with the ring does not queue anywhere in town, not at the mill, not at the doctor.

records.subject: k_senior_date
records.value: Only by inheritance, by marriage, or by standing beside a death — the ring passes on the day its use stops, and the new holder must open a gate and call the same day, in front of the watermaster, or the date drops and the whole basin moves up.

records.subject: k_first_water
records.value: No ring, no cord, nothing. The oldest dates in the basin are held by people who wear nothing at all, and the way you know is that the watermaster stands up.

records.subject: k_first_water
records.value: Nobody now alive has reached it. It is reached only by proving a use older than the register itself, which means producing a witness to a ditch dug before the book was opened, and the last person who tried was found to have paid for the witness.

records.subject: k_no_date
records.value: cr_priority

records.subject: k_junior_date
records.value: cr_priority

records.subject: k_working_date
records.value: cr_priority

records.subject: k_senior_date
records.value: cr_priority

records.subject: s_the_draw
records.value: system

records.subject: s_the_draw
records.value: A commons with no queue at all. Anyone with pipe and a winch can take from underneath, as much as pressure allows, in any order, and nobody can see anybody else taking. The system is numeric because the ground is: feet of pipe, hours of pumping, and a lag measured in years between the taking and the river noticing.

records.subject: s_the_draw
records.value: A stack of pipe in a yard, taller this month than last, and the well-house running all night so the neighbours can hear that the pump is not stopping.

records.subject: s_the_draw
records.value: A bore, a winch, and a driller willing to sign the depth he actually reached rather than the depth he was licensed for.

records.subject: s_the_draw_nature
records.value: The aquifer is slow and it keeps accounts. Everything taken is recorded somewhere in pressure, and it settles up long after the taker is dead.

records.subject: s_the_draw_view
records.value: view

records.subject: s_the_draw_view
records.value: A stack of pipe in a yard, taller this month than last, and the well-house running all night so the neighbours can hear that the pump is not stopping.

records.subject: s_the_draw_view
records.value: The lag table on the office wall is public. The map of which bores are actually connected to the channel is not, and the clerk who redrew it in the last drought has never shown anyone the old one.

records.subject: r_lag
records.value: What a bore takes today, the river misses years from now, and the number of years is set by distance to the channel — three years at a mile, eleven at five, and beyond fifteen miles the table says never and the register taxes it as a gift.

records.subject: r_lag
records.value: A driller pays a tax on a column headed NEVER, and the clerk stamps it without looking up, and neither of them mentions that the table was drawn by a man who has been dead since the last dry.

records.subject: r_lag
records.value: Contracts sold on delivery seven years out, and a whole trade of lag brokers matching a man who needs water now against a river that will be short in a decade.

records.subject: r_lag
records.value: Torts nobody can try. A court must decide whether a bore sunk in 1461 harmed a river in 1468, with no witness alive to the middle, and the standard answer is a fine paid to a fund.

records.subject: r_lag
records.value: Every council meeting is an argument about a harm no living person caused, chaired by people who will not be there when it lands, and the seats are held by whoever can talk longest about seven years from now.

records.subject: r_subsidence
records.value: Ground that has given up its water does not come back up. Over a heavy bore the valley floor drops a hand's width a year and keeps dropping after the bore is capped.

records.subject: r_subsidence
records.value: A door that closed last autumn does not close now, and the man planing the bottom of it has planed it three times and says nothing about why.

records.subject: r_subsidence
records.value: Nothing rigid gets built. Masons work in jointed courses, doors hang loose in oversized frames, and a straight wall is either brand new or the mark of somebody with no bore and no money.

records.subject: r_subsidence
records.value: People measure their houses against a neighbour's wall every spring, and the marks are cut into the stone in a stack going down, which is how you read a family's last twenty years in a doorway.

records.subject: r_subsidence
records.value: The oldest surveys in the register describe a valley that no longer exists at the heights it names, so every old deed is quietly worth less and nobody will say so at auction.

records.subject: r_salt_layer
records.value: Below the sweet water is the old sea. Draw into it and what comes up looks like water and kills the field in three seasons, and the field stays dead.

records.subject: r_salt_layer
records.value: A bucket set on a table, clear, and the driller does not drink it and does not explain, and everyone at the table understands the bore is finished.

records.subject: r_salt_layer
records.value: Basins are poisoned rather than burned. You drill deep on a boundary and walk away, and it works, and it cannot be undone by any peace signed afterwards.

records.subject: r_salt_layer
records.value: A rite for abandoning ground, said at the fence, with the rag tied on at the end of it — and the priests who say it are paid double and never go back.

records.subject: r_salt_layer
records.value: Salt-selling: scraping and trading the crust off a dead field, legal, profitable, and done by people the rest of the basin will not sit near in a public house.

records.subject: cr_depth
records.value: criterion

records.subject: cr_depth
records.value: numeric

records.subject: k_shallow_bore
records.value: A hand pump in a yard, and water in the bucket that tastes of iron and nothing worse. The children drink it.

records.subject: k_shallow_bore
records.value: A season of digging and one licence, and the licence is written junior to every surface date in the basin — which is to say, worthless in law and perfectly adequate in fact.

records.subject: k_deep_bore
records.value: Pipe stacked shoulder-high along the fence like a wall, a winch house with a roof, and a wet ring on the ground that never dries. The house doors have all been rehung to swing again.

records.subject: k_deep_bore
records.value: Paid before the water arrives: the ground under the bore drops a hand's width a year, so the buyer signs away the level of his own floor, and the mason comes back every spring.

records.subject: k_salt_bore
records.value: White crust up the casing and a field beyond it the colour of ash, fenced off, with a rag tied to the wire. Strangers cross the road to avoid the fence.

records.subject: k_salt_bore
records.value: Reached by going past the sweet layer into the old sea, usually on purpose, usually as a threat — and the field it kills is dead for good, including whatever the driller's own children were going to farm.

records.subject: k_shallow_bore
records.value: cr_depth

records.subject: k_deep_bore
records.value: cr_depth

records.subject: a_the_river
records.value: agency

records.subject: a_the_river
records.value: The river itself, which obeys the order and nothing else

records.subject: a_the_river
records.value: Nothing anyone has been able to demonstrate

records.subject: a_the_river
records.value: The whole basin and the mountains behind it

records.subject: a_the_river
records.value: A date, spoken at an open gate, by the person the register names — and nothing else, not need, not thirst, not a child

records.subject: a_the_river
records.value: It serves the order exactly, including on the days that means a family gets none

records.subject: a_the_river
records.value: Water in a furrow turns and walks backwards out of a field while the people standing in it watch.

records.subject: a_the_river_secret
records.value: It has been serving a chain sized to its old volume for sixty years, and the shortfall has always been absorbed at the junior end, which is why no one senior has ever noticed the river changed.

records.subject: a_the_old_sea
records.value: agency

records.subject: a_the_old_sea
records.value: The salt water under the sweet, patient, enormous

records.subject: a_the_old_sea
records.value: Nothing, and rises anyway as the sweet layer is drawn off

records.subject: a_the_old_sea
records.value: Everything below eight hundred feet, everywhere in the basin

records.subject: a_the_old_sea
records.value: Every foot of fresh water taken out brings it a foot closer to fields nobody has drilled

records.subject: a_the_old_sea
records.value: A white line on a casing that is higher this year than last, and a driller measuring it with his hand and saying nothing.

records.subject: a_the_old_sea_secret
records.value: The rise is now general across the basin rather than local to heavy bores, and two people have noticed independently and neither has told the other.

records.subject: y_the_ring
records.value: carrier

records.subject: y_the_ring
records.value: The thin black iron thumb ring of a senior date

records.subject: y_the_ring
records.value: Recognition without speech — the ring is read faster than a paper

records.subject: y_the_ring
records.value: It passes on the day its use stops, which means it is always worn by someone being watched for signs of stopping

records.subject: y_the_ring
records.value: A ring comes into a room and the room reorders itself around it before anyone has spoken.

records.subject: y_the_lag_table
records.value: carrier

records.subject: y_the_lag_table
records.value: A painted board on the office wall giving years-to-river by distance-to-channel

records.subject: y_the_lag_table
records.value: The arithmetic every contract, tax and lawsuit in the basin runs on

records.subject: y_the_lag_table
records.value: Everybody in the room glances up at the same board at the same moment in an argument, and goes on arguing from it.

records.subject: y_the_lag_table_secret
records.value: A third of its distances were redrawn in one night eleven years ago and the original was burned

records.subject: y_the_tally_cord
records.value: carrier

records.subject: y_the_tally_cord
records.value: The belt cord, knotted once per generation of use

records.subject: y_the_tally_cord
records.value: A person's standing, worn where a stranger reads it first

records.subject: y_the_tally_cord
records.value: A cut knot swinging loose at a man's hip while he talks about something else entirely.

records.subject: c_wren_holt
records.value: cast

records.subject: c_wren_holt
records.value: Ditch rider for the watermaster, nineteen, no date of her own, best notebook in the basin

records.subject: c_wren_holt
records.value: A date — any date, the newest and worst one, so long as it is hers and written down

records.subject: c_wren_holt
records.value: The whole ditch system on horseback, twice a week, and the office door

records.subject: c_wren_holt
records.value: Counts out loud. Says numbers before she says opinions.

records.subject: c_wren_holt
records.value: Use, and the absence of it — she can tell a gate opened for show from a gate opened for a crop at forty paces

records.subject: c_wren_holt
records.value: Access. She can open any gate in the basin lawfully and nobody looks at her twice while she does it.

records.subject: c_wren_holt
records.value: Every vacancy she finds is somebody's ruin, and she has to hand it in signed

records.subject: c_wren_holt
records.value: Mud to the knee, a wet notebook in oilcloth, and a habit of standing on the wrong side of a gate so she can see the hinge.

records.subject: c_wren_holt_belief
records.value: That the register is honest bookkeeping done badly, rather than bookkeeping done exactly as intended

records.subject: c_wren_holt_secret
records.value: She has been keeping a private column for two years: every headgate in the basin and the last day it moved. She is four months from a fifth year on three of them.

records.subject: c_ada_serrell
records.value: cast

records.subject: c_ada_serrell
records.value: Watermaster of the Kettle Basin, twenty-two years in the office, holds no date at all by law

records.subject: c_ada_serrell
records.value: To get through one more dry without a curtailment order she cannot enforce

records.subject: c_ada_serrell
records.value: Every gate, every ledger, and the ear of four families who could end the office in a week

records.subject: c_ada_serrell
records.value: Short declaratives. Never explains a decision twice.

records.subject: c_ada_serrell
records.value: A forged use, instantly, and never says so in public

records.subject: c_ada_serrell
records.value: The reading of the board — the order in which names are said, which is the only law anyone here obeys on the day

records.subject: c_ada_serrell
records.value: Signs orders that starve people who are standing in the room

records.subject: c_ada_serrell
records.value: Reads names off a board and stops reading, and does not look up at the stopping.

records.subject: c_ada_serrell_belief
records.value: That the office's neutrality is what keeps the basin from killing itself, when in fact it is the drillers' lag doing it

records.subject: c_ada_serrell_secret
records.value: Refused a senior date twelve years ago, offered as a bribe, and has regretted it every August since

records.subject: c_marius_tebb
records.value: cast

records.subject: c_marius_tebb
records.value: Driller, third generation, sixty feet deeper every year than his licence allows

records.subject: c_marius_tebb
records.value: To get his family off the bottom of a chain they will never climb, by leaving the chain entirely

records.subject: c_marius_tebb
records.value: Ninefold Flat and every yard that has ever wanted a pump

records.subject: c_marius_tebb
records.value: Talks in depths and hours. Turns every moral question into a measurement.

records.subject: c_marius_tebb
records.value: Ground — he can call the sweet layer within ten feet by the smell of the cuttings

records.subject: c_marius_tebb
records.value: Water today for people the board will never reach, at a price and with no queue

records.subject: c_marius_tebb
records.value: Everything he sells now is taken out of a river that will be short in the year his daughter turns twenty

records.subject: c_marius_tebb
records.value: Wet boots in a dry season, and a yard where the pipe wall gets taller between one visit and the next.

records.subject: c_marius_tebb_belief
records.value: That the lag is long enough to be somebody else's problem

records.subject: c_marius_tebb_secret
records.value: His deepest bore on Ninefold is nine hundred feet from the channel, not the four miles the papers say, and he moved the survey mark himself

records.subject: c_orrin_veck
records.value: cast

records.subject: c_orrin_veck
records.value: Holder of the third-oldest date in the basin, eighty-one, cannot walk to a headgate unassisted

records.subject: c_orrin_veck
records.value: To die after the August call and not before it

records.subject: c_orrin_veck
records.value: One gate, four hundred yards, and the whole valley's arithmetic

records.subject: c_orrin_veck
records.value: Whispers, and makes people come close, and uses the closeness.

records.subject: c_orrin_veck
records.value: The exact sound of somebody counting her years

records.subject: c_orrin_veck
records.value: The oldest working call anyone in the basin can actually witness

records.subject: c_orrin_veck
records.value: Every August she spends keeps eleven families junior and she has known all of them since they were born

records.subject: c_orrin_veck
records.value: Carried to a wheel in a chair by two men who hate each other, and the whole road stops to watch the chair go by.

records.subject: c_orrin_veck_belief
records.value: That her nephews are counting the days out of grief

records.subject: c_orrin_veck_secret
records.value: Has not been able to speak the date aloud for two seasons — the dryness took the voice — and has been having it spoken for her by somebody the register would not accept

records.subject: c_ferris_kane
records.value: cast

records.subject: c_ferris_kane
records.value: Vacancy man — buys and sells the knowledge of which rights are about to die

records.subject: c_ferris_kane
records.value: To assemble the fifth years of an entire lateral in one season and take the whole run at once

records.subject: c_ferris_kane
records.value: Four basins, on a good horse, and the back rooms of three registers

records.subject: c_ferris_kane
records.value: Friendly, fast, uses first names immediately.

records.subject: c_ferris_kane
records.value: Despair, and the precise week a family stops trying

records.subject: c_ferris_kane
records.value: Money now, for a notebook

records.subject: c_ferris_kane
records.value: He is never present at the ruin, which is the service he sells himself

records.subject: c_ferris_kane
records.value: Buys the first drink, asks about the weather, writes nothing down while you talk and everything down after.

records.subject: c_ferris_kane_belief
records.value: That what he does is clean because it is exactly what the statute describes

records.subject: c_ferris_kane_secret
records.value: Bought Wren's father's date. The paper is in a box in a town two days away and has been for eleven years.

records.subject: c_teodor_lam
records.value: cast

records.subject: c_teodor_lam
records.value: Office clerk, keeper of the lag table, thirty-one years at the same desk

records.subject: c_teodor_lam
records.value: For nobody to ask him to redraw the table again

records.subject: c_teodor_lam
records.value: One wall, and through it, every contract in the basin

records.subject: c_teodor_lam
records.value: Apologises before disagreeing. Disagrees anyway.

records.subject: c_teodor_lam
records.value: A bore that is nearer the channel than its paper claims, because he did the arithmetic once and could not unsee it

records.subject: c_teodor_lam
records.value: The numbers everyone argues from

records.subject: c_teodor_lam
records.value: Every gift-taxed NEVER he stamps is a debt he personally invented

records.subject: c_teodor_lam
records.value: Stamps a form, blots it, and squares the edge of the paper with two fingers before letting go of it.

records.subject: c_teodor_lam_belief
records.value: That a wrong table that keeps the peace is better than a right one that ends it

records.subject: c_teodor_lam_secret
records.value: He redrew it during the last dry on Serrell's spoken instruction and burned the old sheet, and both of them have decided separately never to mention it

records.subject: p_kettle_basin
records.value: place

records.subject: p_kettle_basin
records.value: The basin — one river, four hundred gates, one book

records.subject: p_kettle_basin
records.value: Every road in it runs beside a ditch and every conversation on those roads pauses at a headgate.

records.subject: p_kettle_basin_secret
records.value: The river carried a third more water in the years the oldest dates were written, and the register has never adjusted for it, which means the senior dates were sized to a river that no longer exists.

records.subject: p_the_headgate_row
records.value: place

records.subject: p_the_headgate_row
records.value: The town street where the main laterals split, and where calls are witnessed

records.subject: p_the_headgate_row
records.value: Everyone. Nobody comes to the row unnoticed.

records.subject: p_the_headgate_row
records.value: Iron wheels in a row, wet stone, and men standing about in the middle of a working day for no reason they will admit.

records.subject: p_ninefold_flat
records.value: place

records.subject: p_ninefold_flat
records.value: The dry ground east of the channel where the bores are

records.subject: p_ninefold_flat
records.value: It is going down a hand's width a year and everyone living on it has agreed not to say so out loud.

records.subject: p_ninefold_flat
records.value: Pipe stacked along fences, winch houses running at night, and a road that used to be level.

records.subject: p_the_salt_quarter
records.value: place

records.subject: p_the_salt_quarter
records.value: Fenced ground west of Ninefold, killed and consecrated

records.subject: p_the_salt_quarter
records.value: Nothing. That is the whole horror of it and the reason the priests will not go back.

records.subject: p_the_salt_quarter
records.value: Rags on the wire, white crust, and hares.

records.subject: i_register_of_dates
records.value: institution

records.subject: i_register_of_dates
records.value: The book, and the office around it

records.subject: i_register_of_dates
records.value: Existence. A right that is not in the book did not happen.

records.subject: i_register_of_dates
records.value: A clerk squares a page with two fingers and a family stops existing.

records.subject: i_register_of_dates_secret
records.value: The index was rebound eleven years ago in a different order and the old binding is gone.

records.subject: i_watermasters_office
records.value: institution

records.subject: i_watermasters_office
records.value: The enforcement arm — one master, four riders, no date

records.subject: i_watermasters_office
records.value: Every gate in the basin, lawfully, at any hour

records.subject: i_watermasters_office
records.value: A board with names on it, read aloud, and the reading stopping.

records.subject: i_watermasters_office_belief
records.value: That neutrality is a position rather than a truce underwritten by people who can end it

records.subject: i_drillers_compact
records.value: institution

records.subject: i_drillers_compact
records.value: A trade association that is legally nothing and practically the second government of the basin

records.subject: i_drillers_compact
records.value: To keep the lag table exactly as wrong as it currently is

records.subject: i_drillers_compact
records.value: Four men agree in a yard, and a survey mark is in a different place by morning.

records.subject: i_church_of_spending

records.subject: i_church_of_spending
records.value: The sect that holds waste is the sacrament

records.subject: i_church_of_spending
records.value: Certified use, ritually witnessed, which the register accepts

records.subject: i_church_of_spending
records.value: A gate opened at midnight onto bare stones, and the sound of it running all night while a room full of people sit and listen.

records.subject: h_the_first_dry
records.value: institution

records.subject: h_the_first_dry
records.value: The founding shortage that made the order necessary and the book possible

records.subject: h_the_first_dry
records.value: Every senior date in the register was written within four years of it, in the same three hands.

records.subject: h_the_first_dry_secret
records.value: The order was not adjudicated. It was agreed at a table by the people who had arrived first, and written down afterwards as though it had been found.

records.subject: h_the_compact_year
records.value: institution

records.subject: h_the_compact_year
records.value: The year the drillers were licensed and written junior to everything

records.subject: h_the_compact_year
records.value: Every bore licence in the basin carries the same year and the same clause, and no clause has ever been enforced.

records.subject: h_the_compact_year_belief
records.value: The basin believes this was a settlement. It was a deferral, and everyone who negotiated it knew the enforcement would arrive after their deaths.

records.subject: h_the_drowning_of_ninefold
records.value: institution

records.subject: h_the_drowning_of_ninefold
records.value: The last wet decade, when Ninefold flooded twice and half its rights lapsed from disuse because there was nothing to prove

records.subject: h_the_drowning_of_ninefold
records.value: The people who got rich on bores are exactly the people who lost their place in the chain to too much water.

records.subject: h_the_drowning_of_ninefold
records.value: An entire lateral of dates all bearing the same forfeiture year, which is why the drillers are all in one place.

records.subject: x_gate_moth
records.value: creature

records.subject: x_gate_moth
records.value: Pale moth of the wetted furrow

records.subject: x_gate_moth
records.value: A man stands in his own field at dusk being crawled on and does not brush them off, because the inspector is watching from the road.

records.subject: x_gate_moth
records.value: Lays only in soil wetted within nine days and never in soil merely rained on, because it needs the ditch silt the river carries. The eggs are visible, countable, and dated by size.

records.subject: x_gate_moth
records.value: Follows the laterals; abundant in a wet year on a called field, entirely absent from a field watered by a bore, which is how the difference between river water and pumped water shows without an instrument.

records.subject: x_gate_moth
records.value: common, and priced anyway

records.subject: x_gate_moth
records.value: Evidence. A register inspector counts eggs on a stalk to certify use, and there is a black trade in moth-boards — frames of eggs raised elsewhere and pressed into a dry furrow the night before an inspection.

records.subject: x_gate_moth
records.value: Comes at dusk in a low sheet, thick enough to walk through, and settles on anything damp including a person.

records.subject: x_bore_worm
records.value: creature

records.subject: x_bore_worm
records.value: Blind white worm of the deep layer

records.subject: x_bore_worm
records.value: Somebody tips a bucket onto a board, and every driller in the yard walks over without being called, and nobody says anything.

records.subject: x_bore_worm
records.value: Lives only at the boundary between the sweet water and the old sea, feeding on the mineral edge where they meet. It cannot survive in either alone.

records.subject: x_bore_worm
records.value: Never seen at the surface except by accident. Its presence in a bucket means the bore has reached exactly the last good foot.

records.subject: x_bore_worm
records.value: rare, and always bad news

records.subject: x_bore_worm
records.value: A warning that arrives too late to be useful and just in time to be used against you — buyers pay drillers to show them the bucket, and drillers pay boys to fish the worms out before the buyer arrives.

records.subject: x_bore_worm
records.value: Dies within a minute in air, curling, and the curl is the shape everyone in the basin recognises.

records.subject: x_salt_hare
records.value: creature

records.subject: x_salt_hare
records.value: Ash-coloured hare of the dead fields

records.subject: x_salt_hare
records.value: A hare sitting still in white ground twenty feet from a man, and the man throwing nothing at it, and walking on.

records.subject: x_salt_hare
records.value: Tolerates the salt crust that kills every crop, licking it for the mineral and taking water only from the fog. Nothing else eats out there and nothing eats it.

records.subject: x_salt_hare
records.value: Appears within two seasons of a field going salt and never before, so its arrival is the boundary marker of a killed field.

records.subject: x_salt_hare
records.value: uncommon

records.subject: x_salt_hare
records.value: Eaten by the poor, and the eating is a public admission of what your ground has become — the meat is fine and the shame is total.

records.subject: x_salt_hare
records.value: Does not run from people. It has never had reason to learn.

records.subject: b_the_witnessed_call
records.value: A caller who has lost the voice can be carried to the wheel and have the date spoken for them by a rider of the watermaster's office, and the register will accept it — once per season, entered in the rider's hand, and the rider's name goes in the book beside the date.

records.subject: b_the_witnessed_call
records.value: One has the standing and no body; the other has the body and no standing. Neither can call alone and both know exactly what the other is worth.

records.subject: b_the_table_and_the_office
records.value: Together they can make a number true — the clerk's arithmetic plus the master's signature turns an estimate into the figure every court in the basin will use — and neither can do it without the other.

records.subject: b_the_table_and_the_office
records.value: A shared decision eleven years old that they have never once discussed, and a mutual, permanent, unspoken hostage-taking.

records.subject: m_holts_date
records.value: Wren's father sold it — not lost it, not forfeited it — to Ferris Kane, eleven years ago, for money that went on a bore that hit salt in its second year. The paper is in a box in a town two days away. Kane has been friendly to her for three years because he is waiting to see whether she works out that the ditch she rides was dug by her grandfather.

records.subject: m_holts_date
records.value: Why does the Holt family, who dug the Ninefold lateral, hold no date?

records.subject: m_holts_date_reveal
records.value: reader

records.subject: m_orrin_last_call
records.value: Her nephew has been speaking it, and the register would void every call he has made if it knew, which would drop the third-oldest date in the basin and move eleven families up a place — including two who are paying him. In August the office learns of it because Wren, having been asked to speak it herself, writes down what she has been asked and hands it in.

records.subject: m_orrin_last_call
records.value: Who has been speaking Orrin Veck's date for her, and what happens in August when she cannot be carried?

records.subject: m_orrin_last_call_reveal
records.value: reader

records.subject: m_pells_lateral
records.value: Not rights. Vacancies in a single unbroken run of one lateral, which under the statute lets a claimant petition to re-found the whole lateral under one new date — the newest and worst date in the basin, attached to more water than any senior date can call, because the lateral's total was sized in a wetter century.

records.subject: m_pells_lateral
records.value: What is Ferris Kane actually assembling out of the fifth years he keeps buying?

records.subject: m_the_wrong_table
records.value: Serrell instructed Lam to redraw fourteen distances in the last dry, to keep the drillers inside the compact and out of the courts. Nine of the fourteen are wrong by more than a mile toward the channel, which means nine bores are already overdue and the shortfall everyone has been blaming on the mountains is being pumped out from under them.

records.subject: m_the_wrong_table
records.value: How wrong is the lag table, and who made it wrong?

records.subject: m_first_water
records.value: It belongs to the register itself — an entry made by the founding clerks in their own institution's name, called once every fourth year at night by the office to keep it from forfeiting. It is senior to every family in the basin, and the office has never used it for anything, because the day it does, the office stops being neutral and becomes the largest landholder in the valley.

records.subject: m_first_water
records.value: Whose is the oldest date in the register, and why has nobody in living memory seen it called?

records.subject: m_where_the_dryness_goes
records.value: Into the river, exactly, and it is the only water in the system that arrives without being taken from someone junior. The oldest rites of the spending church are a garbled memory of a period when calls were made by many people at once for this reason, and the practice ended when the four families worked out that a call made by one person is a call that one person can own.

records.subject: m_where_the_dryness_goes
records.value: Where does the water go that a caller's body loses?

value.label: one dry season in the Kettle Basin

edges.phrase: the register writes a year beside a name
the year stands earlier than every other year on the lateral
a hand on a wet wheel and the year said out loud
the water leaves the fields below and the caller stops sweating
the family below cannot show use for a fifth running year
the rider who watched the gate hands in the notebook
everyone under the cut line moves up one place
and under all of it the bores keep taking a river that will be short in eleven years
